rationale: The Old English lemma (likely a form such as 'tūn') most commonly refers to an enclosed settlement, estate, or urban locality — a physical place smaller than a city. This aligns with town.n.01 (an urban area with a fixed boundary smaller than a city), the primary concrete, locative sense, rather than the collective-people sense (town.n.02) or the administrative-division sense (township.n.01).
